description:
This map displays a detailed Land Cover / Land Use (LCLU) classification of a coastal or estuarine area, including port and urban infrastructure, overlaid on satellite imagery. Various land cover polygons are delineated by yellow outlines and labelled with numerical classification codes.

Three specific areas are highlighted by red circles:
*   Two areas on the left side are classified as `8120`. These correspond to highly modified water courses, canals, or inner harbour areas, as defined in the associated document context. One `8120` polygon depicts an inner harbour basin, while the other is a section of a wide channel or waterway.
*   One large area in the central-right is classified as `8110`, representing a vast open water body, likely a sea, large lake, or estuary.

Other visible classification codes on the map, representing adjacent land and water features, include: `1120` (Port areas), `1121` (Airports), `1122` (Water and wastewater treatment plants), `4100` (Continuous urban fabric), `4110` (Discontinuous urban fabric), `4120` (Industrial or commercial units), `4210` (Non-irrigated arable land), `4220` (Permanently irrigated land), `4230` (Rice fields), `7100` (Aquaculture areas), `7101` (Fishing ports), `7102` (Marinas), `7103` (Shipyards), `9210` (Beaches, dunes and sand plains), `9220` (Sparsely vegetated areas), and `9230` (Salt marshes).

The background imagery shows dark blue for large water bodies, lighter blue/turquoise for smaller or modified water features, and reddish/pink tones for artificial and built-up land surfaces, contrasted with yellowish/greenish tones for other land cover types. No scale bar, compass orientation, legend, or reference year is visible on the map.
